Title: GO APE - TREETOP CHALLENGE PLUS 😃
Summary:
GO APE - TREETOP CHALLENGE PLUS. 😃 Come join me at GO APE - Trent Country Park. Go Ape is approximately a 10 minute walk from Cockfosters Tube station (Piccadilly Line).
Full information about this Go Ape challenge, restrictions, directions, parking etc can be found on the Go Ape website.
Treetop Challenge Plus is Go Ape’s toughest challenge. Crossings called Mind The Gap, Wrecking Balls, Hanging Anchors - The name’s aren’t just for show. This is the toughest high ropes experience at Go Ape. This is a physically demanding activity that requires a good level of fitness and strength. The highest platform is 16m. The longest zip wire is 125m. Please be aware that the Challenge Plus is listed as difficulty level (Extreme) on the Go Ape website. Are you up for the challenge?
The cost is £47.95 which includes a booking fee. Once you have signed up to attend the event on the ODL website, please click on the attached link to Go Ape and make your booking for COCKFOSTERS - SUNDAY 4th OCTOBER at 12:00pm.
We will meet at the Go Ape venue cabin 20 minutes prior to our start time of 12:00pm to have a briefing in preparation for our challenge. Places are limited, so please make your booking immediately after signing up for the ODL event.
Book at
https://goape.co.uk
AN OPTIONAL PUB VISIT AFTER THE END OF THE EVENT FOR REFRESHMENTS AND A BITE TO EAT IF POSSIBLE. 😃

Title: Eight Days a Week(end) of Fun: A Liverpool City Break
Summary:
Come and join us for a weekend break in Liverpool, and enjoy fun times exploring the city!
Liverpool is a vibrant maritime city in North West England, renowned as the birthplace of The Beatles, a powerhouse of football culture, and a hub of rich industrial history. Situated on the Mersey Estuary, it features UNESCO-listed docks, diverse cultural attractions, stunning architecture, and a lively, welcoming atmosphere. Liverpool is the most filmed city outside of London, recent productions filmed here include Batman, Captain America, Sherlock Holmes and Peaky Blinders.
City breaks are less formal and structured than our usual hostel breaks, you’ll have free time or time to do the suggested activities below, but they are all suggestions. City breaks do not have the usual Friday night buffet, (and indeed no food or drink is included in the price) however places to eat as a group will be suggested, or you may wish do your own thing or break into smaller groups.
Itinerary:
Day 1:
Arrive late afternoon on Friday, meet & greet reception before heading off out for dinner and drinks. (Exact restaurant location to be confirmed nearer event date)
Day 2:
Saturday morning, Optional Breakfast at the hostel before we head out for a walking tour exploring the city's maritime heritage. We may stop for lunch at the Royal Albert Docks. If time we might take a trip on the
ferry across the Mersey!
In the afternoon there will be free time to explore the city with an optional visit to the
Beatles Museum
In the evening we will reconvene at the hostel before joining a local OutdoorLads social! Exploring the city's vibrant night life.
Day 3:
Sunday morning, Optional Breakfast at the hostel then free time before checkout - option of a visit to
Liverpool Cathedral
or the
Walker Art Gallery,
Or some adult crazy golf at
Golf Fang Liverpool
Accommodation
Hostel accommodation - ensuite dorm rooms with bunk beds, which will only be shared with other OutdoorLads members attending the city break.
Please note that unlike most of our other hostel events, food is not provided and we will not have sole use of the hostel.
Dogs:
Unfortunately this event is not suitable for dogs. Registered assistance dogs welcome, but please let us know when you book.

Title: European Snow Pride 2027
Summary:
EUROPEAN SNOW PRIDE 2027 - 20-27 MARCH in Tignes
***
European Snow Pride booking is now  open
!! ***
This event is intended to to provide information about snow pride and facilitate (primary via the WhatsApp group) people arranging to share accommodation prior to the event as well as communication on the event.
There is a social organised for the second evening to meet other Outdoorlads whilst there.
However most of the socialising is via the snowpride ski groups and parties and not specifically organised with Outdoorlads as you may have experienced on a typical Outdoorlads event.
This is EUROPE'S BIGGEST GAY FESTIVAL OF  WINTER SPORT & MUSIC with guests coming from all over Europe, North America and beyond.
It takes place in the gay friendly resort of TIGNES and in the snow sure and huge beautiful ski area of Tignes and Val D'Isere!
European Snow Pride features great apres ski on the slopes, with DJs, singers and performers, Fantastic club parties including a giant pool party, a gay pride parade and much more.
A unique opportunity to meet people from all around the world and make new friends!
If you have not attended one of these type of events before they are great fun. In the daytime there are guided groups that you can join for skiing or snowboarding where you will meet lots of other gay guys, and rendezvous restaurants where multiple groups meet for lunch. In the evening there are parties every nite some are themed (fancy dress) and are great fun. In between there is apres ski at the end of the day and the spa (if you have access) .
For more info:-
European Snow Pride website
.
European Snow Pride on facebook
.
PLEASE NOTE THERE ARE TWO EUROPEAN SKIING EVENTS THIS ONE, (EUROPEAN SNOW PRIDE ESP) AND EUROPEAN GAY SKI WEEK  EGSW SO MAKE SURE YOU ARE SIGNING UP TO THE ONE YOU WANT TO ATTEND , ESPECIALLY IF YOUR FRIENDS ARE BOOKED ON ONE. THIS EVENT IS FOR EUROPEAN SNOW PRIDE in TIGNES
There is a WhatsApp group to assist people in communicating to book / share accommodation and to communicate and arrange to meet up whilst there. See the link in the location information below to join.
Please read the info on here carefully and on the ESP website, feel free to ask questions in the whatsapp group.
ACCOMMODATION
There are lots of options see the
European Snow Pride website
for details.
When booking for accommodation is open. I recommend booking ASAP as the best accommodation offers sell out early and the cost increases a little every month !
There are the special offer accoms ranging from approx £500 to £800 these are already really good value as this also includes the event pass and lift pass.
You will need to pay 25% on booking and the remainder 1 month before the event.
I will be booking the deluxe special offer (£798pp (increases monthly)), a lot of the outdoorlads book this as is really good value and it makes shareing with other outdoorlads simple. The apartments are great, it is close to the slopes and it has access to the fantastic spa. This includes both event and lift passes. So just flights, transfers and spending money on top.
The deluxe secial apartments are for 5 people but you don't need to arrange who you are sharing with till later so I recommend booking to secure a place as this will sell out. (There are lots of other options and the non special offer accom is eligible for a small discount see
ODL Discount
). If you are on a tight budget the standard special is great value at £517.
(shareing a small apartment with 4) There is also a comfort special (shareing with 3).
If you have got your own group together then great , if not message on the WhatsApp group , see link in the location information below to join the group, ask if any other outdoorlads are looking to share. With the special offer accom , snowpride will allocate you an apartment with others you request to share with and/or will fill spaces with others on snowpride.
I have shared with others i didn't know in the past and found it a great way to make new friends.
SKIING/SNOWBOARDING
There are daily guided groups for intermediate and advanced skiers/boarders and ski school available for beginners. This year each guided group will be accompanied by an ESP promoter and a professional ski guide from evolution 2.
European Snow Pride Ski options
.
You can hire  your equipment  from ESP also.
EVENT PASS ETC
To participate in the ski groups, a client must either purchase an Event Pass Premium, or an Event Pass Standard plus a supplement for ski and snowboard groups.
The standard includes the evening parties but not the daytime guided ski groups or the pool party.
This makes it more flexible so that if you do not use the guided ski groups or go to the pool party it will be cheaper for you. You can add the pool party or the guided groups to the Standard pass as an optional extra.
If you are intending to do the guided ski groups and pool party then it is more cost effective to get the premium.
Full details on the types of event pass here;:
https://www.europeansnowpride.com/fr/pass-evenement-gay-ski-week/
GETTING THERE
You need to organise your own transport .
See
European Snow Pride travel options
.
When booking flights to the resort the transfers usually leave the airports before 3pm on Saturday and are not likely to arrive back at the airport until after 3pm on the return journey. So please bear this in mind when booking flights. (As in, early flight on arrival and late flight on return. There have been many occasions with a late return transfer as Saturday is change over day for the whole of the french alps! The traffic is usually extremely congested, do not be misled by google travel times that are not for Saturday! Several people have missed flights booked too early in the day.)
To join the Sunday night social odl event
https://www.outdoorlads.com/events/european-snow-pride-social-270321

www.weens.fr
and Andréa Emmanuelli - Lezak
www.andrew-grey.com
and European Snow Pride)

Title: SE500 Golden Autumn in Goring - a two part walk
Summary:
A walk including the glorious colours of autumn through fine woodlands, as well as taking in the best of the vistas of the Thames Valley from grassy hilltops above Goring. Take the challenge of 500 metres of ascent over the walk, or choose half of it if you prefer a more gentle ramble!
This is a 2-part walk:
Part 1 – East of Goring: 12.2km with 269m of ascent with gentler slopes and woods.
Part 2 – West of Goring: 7.1km with 273m of ascent, including steeper slopes and open views.
Total: 19.3km and 542m of ascent.
You can choose at the end of Part 1 whether to continue with Part 2 or complete your walk at the station.
Meeting at Goring and Streatley Station, the morning walk takes in several attractive woodlands and views over farmland from the east of Goring. The rolling hills take the Chiltern Way, which we follow to start with, up over attractive rises giving good vistas west and south across the Thames valley. The morning walk consists of gentler slopes over a longer distance of 12.2km and 269m ascent.
Returning to Goring, Mill Cottage on the right can be seen. This was the house of musician George Michael. The village church is dedicated to St Thomas Becket and dates from the early 13th century.
There is an 18th-century coaching Inn, the Miller of Mansfield, as well as a couple of cafes and several small shops. We shall take lunch here, so you can choose to bring your own and use the benches in Rectory Garden, or get some food in the Inn, cafes, or buy from the shops.
At this point, you will have completed 12.2km. You have the option of continuing your walk to achieve the accolade of completing an SE500, or gracefully bowing out to return to the station, which is a stone's throw away.
After lunch, our walk takes us through the village and across the Thames bridge to the west bank. Originally a ferry, a wooden bridge was first built in 1837, and the weirs form an attractive backdrop. On the west side, the land rises steeply over the grassy slopes of Lardon Chase to the top of Lough Down hill (138m). This is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and has been preserved by the National Trust. Chalk-loving plants have been encouraged, and the slopes support a wide range of flowers and butterflies.
There is then a descent and ascent by a golf course and up into Common Wood. In clearings on the top are three labyrinth mazes formed by shallow mounds of earth and grass. The woods themselves include traditional oaks and chestnut.
Descending back to Goring station after completing the afternoon's 7.1km and 273m of ascent, you have achieved over 500m of ascent in total, over just over 19km - a great achievement helping to burn off around 2,100 calories!
Well behaved dogs are welcome on this walk. You can follow the
route
on OS Maps.

Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Experienced
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an evening at Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre.
"EXPERIENCED" in this instance is those that have previously climbed & can answer YES to all three of these questions:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie in to a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay another climber correctly & confidently?
Please ensure you only sign up for this event if you
satisfy all three of the prerequisites as an experienced (independent) climber!
Never climbed before? Need a refresher on the basics? Answered NO to any of the three questions above? You will need to
attend one of the beginners (supervised) events
instead, where we will happily sign you in to be supervised (two people per leader maximum), show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely! Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event as 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing or would like a refresher, then this is just for you!! If you’ve climbed before, can safely tie into a harness & can competently belay, then there’s plenty of choices of top-rope & lead climbing on offer here.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.
You MUST register via this event page before coming to the centre!

Title: Sheffield bouldering @ Depot Climbing
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at Depot Climbing in Sheffield.
If you’re new to Depot Climbing it’s one of the biggest bouldering centres in Sheffield with plenty of challenging routes that will give you the PUMP your arms crave.
Cards/contactless ONLY  - this venue does not accept cash
If you haven't been to Depot Climbing before, please click
here
to pre-register. Click on the link, scroll down, select 18+ Unsupervised Form and follow the on-screen instructions. Completing the waiver prior to arrival will get you
climbing
faster.
Latest prices can be found
here
.
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by the event leader / venue.
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Sheffield Bouldering @ The Climbing Hanger
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at The Climbing Hanger in Sheffield.
Cards/contactless ONLY  - this venue does not accept cash
If you haven't been to The Hangar before, please click
here
to pre-register. Click on the link, scroll down, select Sheffield and follow the on-screen instructions. Completing the waiver prior to arrival will get you climbing faster.
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by the event leader / venue.
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Indoor Climbing NORTH WALES - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR CLIMBING in NORTH WALES!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Join us for an evening of indoor climbing! Whether you are new to climbing or a seasoned climber, this centre offers something for everyone with a huge selection of routes.
While
climbing
will be the main focus of the event, the centre offer great
bouldering
problems too, so if that's more you're thing, then you're more than welcome to come along and just boulder. But this is also a great chance to meet other members and build lasting friendships. Many OutdoorLads members join through climbing, so if you're new to the group and want to know more, come along and chat over a cuppa during the tea and cake break.
What to expect on your first climb with us?
If you are an experienced climber and have passed the centre's proficiency test, we'll pair you up with a climbing buddy and you'll be out exploring the centre in no time.
If you have never climbed before or think you could do with a refresher, we offer supervised climbing sessions with one of our leaders, subject to availability. That session will focus on introducing you to climbing, making sure you get plenty of time on the wall whilst also showing you how to belay safely. Due to the centre's rules, we are limited in the number of climbers the leader is able to supervise in each session so if you think you may need a supervised session,
please contact the leader before signing up to make sure there is enough space.
As a general guide, if you answer "no" to any of the following questions, you will need to be supervised for the session:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie into a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay and lower down another climber correctly and confidently?
After a few supervised sessions, you should be ready to complete the centre's proficiency test and once that has been passed, you'll be able to climb with the rest of the group.
Everything else you need to know
You will need to register with
The Boardroom Climbing centre
before you start climbing. You only need to do this once and can be done on the day. This also applies if you just want to boulder, just select the relevant options during the registration. If you are a beginner and require a supervised session, the leader will help register you when you are at the centre.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by Mark Mckee
Difficulty & Distance: There is a range of routes of varying difficulty, but there should be something to suit everybody

Title: Malmesbury, Norton and Foxley
Summary:
Join Andrew for a walk starting from the historic town of Malmesbury. This walk is easily accessed from the M4. We will take in parts of the White Walls Way, lots of countryside, usually some llamas and pass through the villages of Norton and Foxley. There will be an optional pub stop at the end of the walk.
Photo credits: photos taken by OutdoorLads members PL1957 and thischarmingman and permission is granted to OutdoorLads for further use.
Dogs are welcome to join us on this event but we do ask the following:
Please appreciate the fact that not everyone is a dog owner or lover- especially when we stop to eat
Please ensure you adhere to the Countryside Code at all times - see
(Keeping Dogs Under Effective Control)
If your dog is uncontrolled and strays in open land frightening other animals or livestock, the leader is supported by the OutdoorLads board of trustees to ask you to leave the event as this is not acceptable behaviour
We cannot guarantee that this route is dog friendly - there may be styles to carry your dog across.
Your dog needs to have the stamina to keep up with the group. This may be an issue on hot days.
Difficulty & Distance: 9-10 miles. 100-120m of height gain

Title: The Tors of Ben Rinnes
Summary:
The
Ben Rinnes
Circular Walk is an 16km loop that ascends the highest freestanding Corbett in Moray, showcasing rugged granite tors and sweeping outstanding views across Speyside.
At the summit is a distinctive rocky outcrop and a trig point, there’s plenty of room to sit and take in the views and have a snack or lunch.
If you're new to mountain walking feel free to drop the leader a personal message to discuss your suitability for the event. We aim to be as inclusive as possible.
Please see
What to Bring
for the essentials in terms of Scottish weather gear.

Title: Old Aberdeen and Beach Circuit
Summary:
A fabulous unexpected mixture of sea front, picturesque riverside and woodland combined with an exploration of the gardens, cobbled streets and ancient buildings, university and cathedral of Old Aberdeen.
This circular route starts from part way along Aberdeen beach - there is free on street parking on the esplanade. Buses can be taken to this point from the city centre or it is possible to walk from the bus and train stations to the sea front.
After our walk we have the option to go for some food before heading home.

Title: Halloween in Beaconsfield
Summary:
Celebrate Halloween in the birthplace of William Penn (founder of the Province of Pennsylvania and the centre of Quakerism).  The hamlet of Jordans will be our base for the weekend as we explore this little slice of Buckinghamshire.
We will stay at YHA Jordans, just a 25 minute drive from Amersham, at the end of the Metropolitan Line.  The single storey hostel sleeps 18 in 4 bedrooms (2 four bed and 2 five bed - all rooms open directly to the outdoors) and will be
dog-friendly
for this weekend.
Friday afternoon / evening
arrive anytime after 16.00, find a bed and get ready to enjoy a build-your-own taco bar with all the fixings.  Feel free to contribute to dessert! This is a great time to catch up with friends old and new!
Saturday
breakfast will be my "famous" chocolate brioche eggy bread, as well as traditional brekkie offerings.  We will then head out on this
12 mile circular
into the village of Amersham and back.  Lunch will be at
The Saracen's Head
, a coaching inn built in the early 1530's and rumoured to be haunted!  All food and drink is payable individually and vegetarian / gluten-free options are available.
Upon return to the hostel there will be time to rest and relax before a full-blown build-your-own fajita bar!  The evening will consist of board and card games and perhaps a Halloween-themed movie!!
Sunday
will see us leaving by 10.00 so breakfast will be a general continental set up.
If this is your first event, don't be put off if you lack some of the necessary equipment; just message me on
chris.keivit@outdoorlads.com
and we will see what can be worked out!
Good to Know....
Bedding
Traditional "YHA bedding" is provided (a duvet, mattress cover and pillow) but personal pillows and sheets always add to the comfort level..
Dogs
This is a dog friendly event (maximum of two well behaved furry friends) so please email
support@outdoorlads.com
prior to booking if you intend to bring your pooch with you.
Photos provided courtesy of
www.unsplash.com
and ODL members.
Difficulty & Distance: A relaxing Halloween hostel weekend

Title: Dark Nights and Big Mountain Days
Summary:
A weekend in the most exciting corner of North Wales, over the Halloween weekend.
In this location in the South of Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park, you are surrounded by some of the most majestic mountains and away from the crowds.
Our accommodation for the weekend is a private hostel with basic facilities. But it is clean, cosy and we will make it warm and welcoming.
There is a pub within easy walking distance and the choice of mountain walks is dazzling.
Some of the pictures show the Nantlle Ridge which is one of the most respected and renowned ridge day walks in the National Park.
So, if you aren’t frightened of the dark and you’re up for some serious mountain walking adventures, this is the weekend for you.
Please note that you need to bring your own bedding to this venue (although a pillow is provided - it will need a pillowcase)
Dogs:
This event is not suitable for dogs.
Photos
: Taken by L Russell and used by OutdoorLads with full permission.
Difficulty & Distance: This is a proper mountain environment and all walk options will be strenuous but achievable for anyone with reasonable fitness and the right kit

Title: An Illuminating Suppertime in Blackpool
Summary:
Join Andy and the OutdoorLads for a relaxed and enjoyable Friday evening supper in the heart of Blackpool!
This is a fun, friendly, and flexible social evening designed around whatever the group would most enjoy. Whether you're visiting Blackpool for the weekend's events that are running, or simply looking for an opportunity to meet new people, this promises to be a wonderful way to start the weekend.
We'll begin by taking a leisurely stroll along Blackpool's famous promenade, soaking up the lively atmosphere of one of Britain's most iconic seaside destinations. As we wander beside the coastline, there will be plenty of opportunities to chat, enjoy the sea views, watch the world go by, and admire the illuminations and attractions that make Blackpool such a vibrant place to visit.
After our walk, we'll head into town to find somewhere for a well-earned drink and supper. Blackpool's food scene has evolved dramatically in recent years, with a growing selection of restaurants, cafés, gastropubs, and independent eateries offering cuisine from around the world. From traditional favourites to exciting contemporary dining experiences, there is something to suit every taste and budget.
The evening is as much about the company as it is about the food. Sharing a meal together provides the perfect opportunity to relax, swap stories, make new friends, and enjoy the welcoming and inclusive atmosphere that OutdoorLads events are known for. Whether you're a regular attendee or joining us for the first time, you'll find a warm welcome and plenty of good conversation.
So come along and join us for a sociable evening of seaside strolling, great food, refreshing drinks, and excellent company as we discover some of Blackpool's newest and most exciting places to eat.
TRAVEL:
There are plenty of car parks in Blackpool, and there is free parking in the streets. A charge applies if you wish to park on the prom. Blackpool North and Blackpool South train stations are easily accessible. There are, of course, the trams which you can use.
DRESS CODE:
Smart casual clothing. No tracksuit bottoms please !

Title: Blackpool parkrun
Summary:
For those of you who enjoy your weekly parkrun fix, we'll be heading to
Blackpool parkrun
before the
Gay Illuminations Day Stroll
and
Blackpool Illuminations Social
later the same day. If you've not heard of it, parkrun is a free, weekly, timed 5k event that takes place every Saturday at locations across the world.
We will meet at 8.45am by the parkrun sign for a group photo. I'll be wearing a red parkrun t-shirt, and you're welcome to wear any OutdoorLads merchandise. You can register for parkrun and get your own barcode from
www.parkrun.org.uk
to scan at the end of your run to record your finish time if you wish. However, you do not need to do this to take part in the run if you don't want to.
Course description:
The course is 5k long, run on tarmac, gravel and trail paths. It’s an almost two lap, anti-clockwise course that is mainly flat. Some sections of the course may accumulate mud, leaves and puddles after rain.
The course starts on the tarmac path south of the clock tower between the netball courts and all weather football pitches. The actual start is parallel to the middle of three floodlights on the left. After the start the route takes the first path on the left. It then turns left adjacent to a black bin and passes by the BMX track which will be on your right. Follow the path towards the model village before exiting the park to turn left along the footpath of East Park Drive.
At the next entrance to the park we re-enter the park and make an immediate right turn onto the woodland trail which is twisty and in places narrow. We follow the lakeside shore for a while before making a right and left turn to take us away from the shore. Eventually the route re-joins the network of tarmac paths. Take the second path on the right and heads towards the crazy golf course. The course turns left here and makes a short descent to follow the Lakeside Promenade towards the bandstand.
The route goes left across the front of the bandstand and up the gravel slope on the right. Here it continues around on the first path to the right. When you catch sight of the rose garden on your left take the sharp turn to the left then turn sharp right to follow the right hand outer path of the rose garden with tennis courts on your right. At the pavillion turn right towards the clock tower. At the clock tower turn left and cross the start line to commence the second lap which is the same as the first lap until you reach the rose garden for the second time. To finish you follow the centre path in the rose garden. The course ends in-between the first two bushes in the garden.
On occasion parkruns can be cancelled due to the weather or lack of volunteers. Should this happen I will try to contact members as soon as I can.
Photos taken by OutdoorLads members who have given us permission to use them.
Difficulty & Distance: 5k parkrun

Title: Bouldering MANCHESTER - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR BOULDERING in Manchester!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Bouldering is a form of climbing that focuses on shorter "problems" emphasising technique, balance, body positioning, and sometimes power, rather than long, high routes. Without the need for ropes, harnesses, and belaying, bouldering is an accessible activity for newcomers and is often considered the "purest" form of climbing.
Bouldering offers a wide range of benefits, including:
Physical:
Improved strength, tone, balance, power, and coordination.
Mental:
Enhanced problem-solving, focus, concentration, and body awareness.
Emotional:
Relaxation, a sense of achievement, and a feeling of mind-body connection.
Bouldering is also a fantastic way to meet new people and build lasting friendships, as it's an inherently social sport where climbers share tips and strategies to conquer the routes.
New to Bouldering?
If you're new to bouldering, it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader to learn the basics of safe bouldering. The leader can then introduce you to the rest of the group where you can refine your newly learnt skills in a social environment.
Experienced Boulderer?
If you’re new to climbing with ODL, the leader will help to introduce you to the rest of the group so you can explore the centre together.
You are responsible for your own safety and actions while bouldering. Please use your own judgement when accepting advice from OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers, regardless of your bouldering experience.
Ready to boulder?
You will need to sign up on the ODL event page. We would ask you to do this each time so that the leader has access to important information
If you are not already registered with Rock Over Climbing, please do so
here
to save time when you arrive. You only need to do this once.
When you arrive at the centre you will need to pay for entry and hire climbing shoes if you don't own a pair. ODL members benefit from the concessionary rate so please mention this when paying.
Get bouldering! You’ll find most of the group already bouldering so feel free to join them. If you’re new to bouldering with ODL, the leader will be looking out for you so if you spot them, please go speak with them first.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by
Sieh
and joenellist.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: LONDON BOULDERING Thursday Evening - Beginners Welcome! 😃
Summary:
Come and join OutdoorLads for some bouldering in central London!
This event is for members of all levels of experience and all are welcome to come along to any of the sessions.
Bouldering is a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems', as they are referred to, tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes the activities excellent for newcomers to the sport.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
Do I need a guided session?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Independent boulderer?
As above all attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you are at all times responsible  for your own safety actions and involvement. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.

Title: Jesmond Dene parkrun
Summary:
For those of you who enjoy your weekly parkrun fix, we'll be heading to
Jesmond Dene parkrun
before the OutdoorLads
NE&Y Leaders Gathering
and
Newcastle Autumn Social
later the same day. If you've not heard of it, parkrun is a free, weekly, timed 5k event that takes place every Saturday at locations across the world.
We will meet at 8.45am by the parkrun sign for a group photo. I'll be wearing a red parkrun t-shirt, but feel free to wear any OutdoorLads merchandise. You can register for parkrun and get your own barcode from
www.parkrun.org.uk
to scan at the end of your run to record your finish time if you wish. However, you do not need to do this to take part in the run if you don't want to.
Course description:
The course is 5k long, run entirely on tarmac paths. Some sections of the course may accumulate mud, leaves and puddles after rain.
The course starts and finishes just above Millfield House near Pet’s Corner and runs through the dene on a path parallel to Red Walk. It follows a few left and right turns, taking you round to 21 steps and a steep hill up to Paddy Freeman’s Park. There is a big loop followed by a small loop of this park before descending a steep hill and back along the path to the finish.
On occasion parkruns can be cancelled due to the weather or lack of volunteers. Should this happen I will try to contact members as soon as I can.

Title: On the Slopes of Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) - Eryri
Summary:
PLEASE CHECK YOUR MESSAGES.  THERE HAS BEEN SOME SLIGHT CHANGES TO THE EVENT.
Join us for a weekend in the
Nant Gwynant
area, staying in a
recently renovated mountain bunkhouse
beneath the southern slopes of
Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon)
.
Nant Gwynant is one of the main gateways into southern Eryri (Snowdonia). The
Watkin Path starts directly outside the front door
, while Beddgelert, the Glaslyn valley and the lakes of Nant Gwynant are all within easy reach. The area combines mountains, lakes, rivers, woodland and the remains of Eryri's industrial past, making it an excellent base for a walking weekend.
One of the biggest advantages of staying here is that
all walks will start directly from the bunkhouse
, allowing us to leave the cars behind for the weekend and explore the area on foot.
We'll arrive on Friday evening, with our traditional OutdoorLads buffet to start the weekend. Breakfasts are included on both mornings, along with a shared evening meal on Saturday.
Walking
The walks offered will depend on the leaders available for the weekend.
If sufficient Mountain Walk Leaders are available, we hope to offer mountain walks on both days. Possible routes include
Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon)
via the Watkin Path and
Cnicht
.
If mountain leadership isn't available, we'll instead make use of the extensive network of paths around Nant Gwynant, Beddgelert and the Glaslyn valley. These lower-level routes still provide access to some of the best scenery in Eryri without venturing onto the higher mountains.
Final walk details will be confirmed once the event attendance is known.
The Bunkhouse
Our base for the weekend is a traditional stone mountain bunkhouse that has recently undergone a major refurbishment. It combines modern facilities with the character of a historic mountain property, creating an excellent base for exploring this part of Eryri.
Facilities include comfortable bunk rooms, a well-equipped kitchen, dining area, sitting room with a wood-burning stove, drying room and modern shower facilities. With the Watkin Path passing the front door, we can simply step outside and start walking.
The Area
The bunkhouse is ideally located for exploring the Nant Gwynant area. Nearby are the
Watkin waterfalls
,
Llyn Dinas
,
Llyn Gwynant
,
Cwm Llan
and the
Glaslyn
river, while
Beddgelert
can be reached on foot along public footpaths.
The surrounding area includes some of Eryri's best-known mountains, including
Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon)
,
Cnicht
,
Moel Hebog
and the
Nantlle Ridge
, alongside quieter valleys and woodland for lower-level walks.
Parking
Parking at the bunkhouse is available for around eight vehicles. The nearest public parking is in Beddgelert, approximately 3.5 miles away. Car sharing may therefore be required for this event. If you can offer lifts, or would like one, please indicate this by messaging  the event leader once you have booked, so we can coordinate transport before the weekend. We will get everyone there somehow!
Staying on Sunday Night
The event officially finishes on Sunday afternoon. However, you're welcome to stay for a third night on Sunday at no additional cost if you'd like to make more of the weekend and reduce the amount of travelling.
If you choose to stay, there will usually be enough food available for breakfast on Monday morning, but an evening meal on Sunday is not included. You'll therefore need to provide your own meal, either by cooking at the bunkhouse or eating out locally.
Please let the leader know nearer the time if you intend to stay on Sunday night. A walk will still be offered on the Sunday before the event finishes.

There will be the leaders dog on this event

Title: The Wild Side of Welford: Field, Furrow & Towpath
Summary:
The ancient coaching village of
Welford
sits on the extreme edge of
Northamptonshire
– tight up against the border with
Leicestershire
.
Lying half way between Northampton and Leicester, Welford became an important resting place for stage coaches – at one time having seven Inns or Coaching Houses along the present High Street. These days, the village is very easily accessible - just a mile or so from junction 1 of the A14.
Our walk begins with arguably the stand-out selfie opportunity of the year. A chance to get a picture taken alongside
Postman Pat
and his black and white cat! During the meticulous research phase of preparing this walk(!), I couldn't find a reason why Pat and Jess are celebrated here in this way – especially since the postie's round is miles away in Cumbria! Anyway, let's not quibble – Welford is proud to celebrate these iconic characters and they've become a popular attraction.
Pat points the way to our first path which takes us around the periphery of the village before we head off across the fields to the
Grand Union Canal
.
Joining the towpath, we soon skirt around the site of the medieval village of
Downton
. Don't get too excited – the history of this village is largely unknown, having been completely deserted by the early 18th century. Both the canal construction and the modern mechanised plough have taken their toll. Spoiler alert: nothing remains!
We'll have just over 2 miles to enjoy this particularly tranquil stretch of the Grand Union Canal before we join a brief section of the
Jurassic Way
– a long distance path which connects Banbury in Oxfordshire with Stamford in Lincolnshire, largely following an ancient ridgeway traversing Britain.
This path takes us up into the
Hemplow Hills
and a beautiful wooded area. As we emerge from the trees, we'll pause for a picnic lunch.
A series of footpaths and bridleways take us east and then north until we hit the upper reaches of the
River Avon
. We're very close to the river's source near
Naseby
and so, at this point, the Avon is nothing more than a babbling brook. Hard to believe that after Rugby and Warwick, these waters flow through the iconic tourist scene at Stratford before running past Evesham to join the Severn near Tewkesbury.
We'll walk alongside the Avon across the final few fields before Postman Pat welcomes us back to
Welford
.
For those that want to stay on, we have the option to walk a couple of hundred yards through Welford's charming Pocket Park to cross over the border into Leicestershire and enjoy refreshments at the
Wharf Inn
.
Dogs are welcome:
Our walk includes field paths, bridleways, village streets and we cross one minor A road. We may encounter sheep, lambs, cows or horses and there are a few fields where landowner signs request dogs on a lead.
Waiting List:
If there are no places left on this event, please join the waiting list as people frequently drop out during the week before an event, and you are very likely to get a place.
Don't waste that space!

, or go to the

section of the website for more information.

You can bookmark our upcoming events list via the short link:
https://outdoorlads.events/central
.

OutdoorLads

Title: Chislehurst and its Caves: Daylight Shunned and Daylight Saved on My 300th Lead
Summary:
As this event includes an exclusive guided
tour of Chislehurst Caves
, it is £13 for all members.
The clocks actually go back on Sunday 25th October, but creepy, chilly Chislehurst Caves couldn't take our booking for a guided tour then. The day that British Summer Time ended would have been so appropriate, because on the tour of the town and fields of Chislehurst that we'll do after our tour of the caves, we'll encounter the grave of the man who did most to bring about Daylight Saving, one William Willett. While out on the remarkably rural green spaces in between the handsome houses, we'll also encounter Malcolm Campbell, Napoleon III and Charles de Gaulle. The dwindling daylight of Autumn will be a motif of the walk, shunned in the caves, saved in the history and savoured on the heaths.
The sights:
Chislehurst:
A wooded, affluent suburb with medieval origins. Its historic core centres on the High Street and St Nicholas’s Church, whose churchyard contains the burials of William Willett, the advocate of daylight saving, and Sir Malcolm Campbell, the land- and water-speed record holder. The village expanded rapidly after the railway arrived in 1865, attracting substantial Victorian houses and wealthy City residents. We'll also glimpse Camden Place, the home of the French Emperor Napoleon III from 1871 to 1873. Napoleon staged a coup d’état in 1851 against Napoleon I's nephew, Louis-Napoleon, overthrowing the Second Republic's constitutional government, proclaiming himself Emperor Napoleon III and establishing the Second French Empire. Following personal defeat during the Franco-Prussian War at the Battle of Sedan in 1870, he was overthrown and the Third Republic was proclaimed. Captured by the Prussians, he went into exile in Britain, settling at Chislehurst, where he died in 1873. His Empress, Eugénie, lived on occasionally there, dying in 1920.
Chislehurst Caves
:
A 22-mile labyrinth of artificial chalk workings, excavated from the C18 onwards for chalk, lime and flint, the chalk was used agriculturally and the flint for firearm triggers. Opened as a visitor attraction in 1900, the atmospheric tunnels soon acquired legends and ghost stories, but their most important use came during the Second World War, when they became a vast deep air-raid shelter accommodating up to 15,000 people, some of whom continued to live underground after their homes had been destroyed. By November 1940, special evening trains ran from Cannon Street to Chislehurst to cope with the crowds. Hitler knew about them and Lord Haw-Haw referred to them, ominously warning that the Germans 'knew about the rats living underground in Kent' and that they 'were coming to get them'. Later used for mushroom cultivation and as a concert venue, with David Bowie, Pink Floyd and Jimi Hendrix performing there in the 1960s and 1970s. The carvings made by New Zealand-born artist Sandy Brown, who worked alone underground, and until 1985 a £5 challenge was offered to anyone willing to spend the night alone in the caves. One policeman succeeded by spending the night carving a figure into the wall, but afterwards said he would never repeat the experience, while another challenger was found unconscious and unable to explain what had happened. They were used as a filming location for
Doctor Who
’s 1972 serial
The Mutants
, in which the Third Doctor and Jo Grant help the Solonians overthrow the evil Marshal. We’re booked in for an exclusive 50-minute tour covering one mile, not 22!. See the video
here
.
Scadbury Park:
A rare survival of a medieval rural landscape within Greater London, encompassing woodland, meadows, farmland and historic parkland. Little-remains of the moated medieval manor house (foundations, cellars, undercroft, fishponds and traces of a bridge) which belonged to the Walsingham family from 1424, including Sir Francis Walsingham, Elizabeth I’s celebrated spymaster. Its ancient woodland, hedgerows and wetland habitats are of considerable ecological importance.
Petts Wood:
An inter-war garden suburb, developed after 1928. Detached and semi-detached houses, mature gardens and tree-lined streets. The adjoining woodland, protected from development by the National Trust, is central to its identity. Leader of the Free French and future President of France Charles de Gaulle and his family lived briefly at 41 Birchwood Road in 1940, during his wartime exile, before bombing prompted their move to Shropshire.
William Willett Memorial:
A 1927 memorial sundial to builder William Willett (1856-1915), who campaigned for daylight saving, stands in the woodland. Set to British Summer Time, it bears the apt inscription,
“I only tell the summer hours”.
Willett became Britain’s leading campaigner for daylight saving. The idea reportedly came to him during an early-morning ride near Petts Wood, when he noticed people sleeping despite the summer daylight. In 1907 he published
The Waste of Daylight
, proposing that clocks should advance progressively in spring and revert in autumn, allowing more evening daylight and reducing artificial-light consumption. Despite support from Winston Churchill, his proposals failed in Parliament. Willett died in 1915 without seeing them adopted. Britain introduced British Summer Time in 1916, partly to conserve coal during the First World War.
The
route
(please click to see it at the Ordnance Survey)
:
We'll walk along Station Approach to Old Hill before turning down Forest Close to go to the caves. Back on Old Hill, we'll walk to the Bromley Road, see Camden Place, then cross Chislehurst Common to Centre Common Road. We'll go up the High Street, turn right up Park Road, the take an alleyway to Foxbury, and go in a loop round to the Cemetery, cross the A222 and follow a footpath across Scadbury Park. We'll then follow the London Loop and Manor Park Road southwest to Chislehurst Church and the Tiger's Head. We'll then follow Hawkwood Lane and Botany Bay Lane before veering east to resume the London Loop, only leaving it to see Birchwood Road. Re-emerging into an open space, we'll follow Kyd Brook and Gosshill Road back to Station Approach.

Title: Festive Grandeur at Knightshayes Court
Summary:
Kick off the festive season with a scenic, varied winter day walk on the Devon/Somerset border! Starting directly from the National Trust’s grand
Knightshayes Court
estate, our circular route weaves together peaceful estate parkland, the River Exe valley, the historic Grand Western Canal, and quiet rolling country lanes through charming hamlets.
We’ll finish our hike back at Knightshayes with plenty of time in the afternoon to warm up with hot drinks, festive treats, and explore the spectacular Victorian Gothic mansion dressed in its full Christmas glory.
Event Overview
Duration:
~4 to 4.5 hours (excluding post-walk estate visit)
Distance:
~8.5 miles (13.5 km)
Difficulty:
Moderate. A mix of estate trails, flat canal towpath, gentle rural ascents, and quiet paved country lanes.
Pace:
Social and steady, with stops for photos and a packed lunch on the trail.
The Route Highlights
Knightshayes Parkland & Bolham:
Leaving the estate grounds, we head west through ancient parkland before dropping down towards the picturesque village of Bolham.
Grand Western Canal:
Joining the tranquil, flat towpath at the edge of Tiverton, following the historic waterway eastward toward Copplestone.
Devon Countryside & Hamlets:
Turning north through rolling countryside, passing Craze Lowman, Peadhill, and the village of Chevithorne before looping back through Chettiscombe.
Estate Return:
Entering the Knightshayes grounds through the tranquil wooded trails to complete the loop.
Afternoon: Knightshayes Christmas Festivities
After completing the walk, we will head into the courtyard to enjoy a well-deserved hot drink, mince pie, or festive treat from the Stables Café. You’ll then have the rest of the afternoon free to tour the
Knightshayes Victorian mansion

Note: Access to the estate grounds and car park is free for National Trust members (remember to bring your NT card!). Non-members can pay for parking/entry on the day.

Title: Wednesday Corndon Round
Summary:
Join Dan for a lovely mid-week leg stretcher on the border of mid-Wales and England.
We will quickly leave the small town behind us by hopping into fields and farmland and steadily heading uphill through the hamlet of Old Church Stoke, skirting the edges of Roundton Hill Nature Reserve on our way up to our first summit, Lan Fawr (426m).
Dropping down and through a small plantation we climb steeply again to the trig point at Corndon Hill (513m) and have some lunch on our highest summit of the day with great views over to Stiperstones, the Wrekin, Long Mynd, the Berwyns and even Eryri on a good day.
Down into a shallow valley for a little shade and shelter then up again for another glorious view from the top of the severe slopes of Roundton (370m) before coming down and around the side of Todleth Hill and back to Churchstoke for a spot of cake at the cafe.
This walk is roughly
12 km/7.5 miles
, on footpaths, muddy fields and lots of stiles with a total ascent of
691m
.
Well-behaved OutdoorDogs are very welcome but please ensure they are adequately prepared for all conditions just as much as you are. Note: Leads will be required in areas with livestock, and we will be crossing awkward stiles frequently.

Title: Rowsley to Matlock Bath - DVH Way Section 4
Summary:
The Derwent Valley Trust
was set up in 1996 to promote the history, arts, wildlife and leisure opportunities that surround the river Derwent along its 55 mile course through Derbyshire.
The Derwent Valley Heritage Way
takes us from Ladybower Reservoir in the Peak District National Park to its end at Derwent Mouth where it flows into the River Trent near Shardlow. The Duke of Devonshire opened the walk at Chatsworth House in 2003.
The route takes us through the Chatsworth estate, Derbyshire dales, towns, villages, canals and many points of interests through the
Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site
. There are plenty of pubs and tea shops for refreshments along the way. The route follows the riverside path through Derby City and continues southeastwards to the historic inland port of Shardlow. Journey’s end is at Derwent Mouth where the Derwent flows into the River Trent.
The route is divided into eight sections of between  ~13 km (8 miles) and ~17 km (10.5 miles), each with a clear public transport solution. All, except the first section, are linear routes. We park at the end, travel to the start, and walk back to our cars. Sections 5, 6, 7 are brilliantly served by the East Midlands Railway Derwent Valley Line
(Derby–Matlock, hourly), which runs almost parallel to the trail the whole way. For sections (2, 3, 4 and 8), we use local buses.
Each section is a walk in itself. Join one or more, as you wish, or walk all eight sections to complete the whole route through Derbyshire. Please ask other attendees for a lift if you need one.
Section 4 - Rowsley to Matlock Bath ~14 km (8.7 miles) Total ascent 190 m (623 ft)
Near the start of the walk we visit the
tea rooms at Rowsley South Station
. This is the northernmost station of the Peak Rail Heritage Railway, a preserved section of the former Midland Railway line, once connecting Manchester Central and London St Pancras. Closed in 1968, this historic route now operates a 4-mile stretch between Rowsley South and Matlock. The Trust aims to re-open the line from Matlock to Bakewell.
From Rowsley the Way follows the River Derwent closely at first then visits the quiet, attractive settlements of Churchtown. We will pause at St Helen’s Church where there is a 1,000-year-old yew tree in the churchyard.
The route leaves the riverside at Darley Bridge and Oaker before again running alongside the river to enter Matlock.
Matlock station is the northernmost terminus for mainline train services on the Derwent Valley Line from Derby. We cross over Matlock Bridge to Hall Leys Park, founded in 1911, where toilets and refreshments are available.
From the park we head towards the parish church of St Giles in the Old Matlock district. Pic Tor Recreation Ground takes us to the climb up to
High Tor
(Giddy Edge) for spectacular views into the valley before we descend through woods back to the river and in to Matlock Bath.

Title: Autumn Ayots and Shaw's Corner
Summary:
Join Alex for this 11-mile autumnal amble around assorted Ayots.
We will meet at Welwyn North station and head southwest into the village of Digswell, dominated by a large viaduct carrying the East Coast Mainline across the valley of the River Mimram. We will pass the parish church of St John the Evangelist and Digswell Hall before entering Sherrardspark Wood, a large nature reserve on the edge of Welwyn Garden City.
Here we will turn west through the small settlements of Ayot Green and Ayot Little Green and follow the Ayot Greenway, a disused railway line now used as a track for walkers and cyclists. We will skirt fields and woodlands as our route takes us northwest towards the village of Ayot St Lawrence.
On arrival in the village we will pass Shaw's Corner, the home of the playwright George Bernard Shaw, author of
Pygmalion
and
St Joan
, and recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1925. We will stop for lunch in the classical church of St Lawrence built in 1778 as a replacement for the 12th-century original.
After lunch we will turn east, passing the ruins of the old church and heading out into more open countryside. Our route will take us through historic Welwyn, the original settlement of that name before the establishment of the much larger garden city in 1920, passing the parish church of St Mary the Virgin.
On leaving Welwyn we will cross more farmland and woodland before arriving back at at station, which has a convenient pub just next door.

Title: Bronzed Beeches and Possible Pannage Piggies
Summary:
Join me on this walk through some of the loveliest bits of the New Forest National Park, away from the crowds, across the wide open spaces of the heathlands and through ancient woodlands that should be in their autumn finery.
We will be well away from the privately owned, enclosed areas are the National Park, with the entire walk within the 'perambulation boundary' of the Forest, which is the area where commoners' livestock are free to roam. Therefore I can confidently guarantee we will see plenty of the iconic New Forest ponies, quite likely some cattle and donkeys, but with a little luck we may also spot families of pigs out foraging freely.
Pannage is an ancient practice that is still used today by New Forest Commoners, who turn out their pigs into the Forest during the season. The pannage season usually lasts around 60 days, between September to November. The start and finish of it is decided by the
Verderers of the New Forest
, with the season starting on the 14th September this year. One of the primary reasons for pannage is that fallen green acorns contain high levels of tannic acid, which is poisonous and potentially fatal to the area's free-roaming ponies and cattle. The pigs, however, will gladly hoover them up with no ill effect!
Our
route
heads south out towards one of the more elevated parts of the Forest on Bratley Plain with extensive views all around, and particularly to Cranborne Chase in the NW. After passing under the A31, we'll pass by the area that was so badly affected by the big wildfire in early August. Fortunately spared was the peaceful, photogenic spot of Soarley Beeches, an isolated, atmospheric clump of ancient, gnarled beech trees set out on the open heath, on a slope facing towards the distant Solent and the Isle of Wight.
We'll then head down to pick up the cycle track which climbs back up to Bolderwood. The Canadian War Memorial sits by the roadside at the top of the hill, honouring Canadian troops who gathered there for church services before heading to Juno Beach for the D-Day landings on June 6, 1944. Continuing north, we'll dip back under the A31 again and continue on to Ocknell Pond and Cadman's Pool where we'll take a break for lunch.
On from there, we'll head down through mature ancient woodlands and then emerge into hamlet of Fritham where it would be rude not to stop for a drink at the Royal Oak. The final stretch keeps the high ground for a while over Fritham Plain then, with us perhaps starting to tire a little, decending the appropriately named Ragged Boys Hill. Following the line of Dockens Water stream will lead us back to our start point at the High Corner Inn.
Dogs
well-behaved dogs are welcome on the walk, but must be under close control at all times and on a lead in the vicinity of livestock or where wildlife may be disturbed. Also note that the entirity of this walk will be in areas where livestock is free-roaming, and you will need to confident that your dog will remain under control if we encounter animals it may not be accustomed to, such as pigs. Hot weather may also make it inappropriate to bring a dog for such a distance during the middle of the day.

Title: London Indoor Climbing Evening - All abilities- Beginners welcome
Summary:
Come join OutdoorLads for indoor climbing in North London!
At the biggest climbing centre in North London, there are 450 routes over 95 lines set across 1000 square metres of wall offering top-roping, lead climbing and bouldering on a wide range of slabs, cracks, overhangs, off-widths and chimneys - there really is something to suit every level of climbing ability!
I've never climbed before, can I come along? YES- but contact the Event Leader (see below)!
Supervised sessions
If you're unsure whether you need to be signed in as a supervised climber or not, if you answer
NO
to any of the following three questions, then you will need to arrange to be supervised. If you can answer YES to all these questions, you can sign up to this event as an unsupervised climber:
1. Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
2. Can you tie yourself to the end of a rope using the correct knots?
3. Can you belay another climber correctly and confidently?
To come along, you will need to register via this event page, and to climb you will need to pay an entry fee directly to the centre when you arrive.
See below.
Also to make climbing more accessible, the Castle has kindly provided us with some group benefits:
If you are climbing with the group, tell the reception when paying for entry and you will get the concession rate. That's £12.50 instead of £18 for full price entry!
For those in need of financial support, we have access to some free entries. Speak to the Event Leader about how this works. We need to provide to the Castle some basic details (name, DoB, email) 48 hours before the session.
Tokens are available for free shoe or harness hire. We have two ODL harnesses that we can lend beginners climbing with the group- so get the free hire shoes!
NOTE: If you are climbing with us for the first time,
either as an experienced climber or beginner,
please send a note to the Event Leader
telling them about your experience and goals.
There is a limit to the number of beginners that we can accommodate at each session. Each beginner needs to be supervised so we  need to ensure there are enough experienced climbings to help you out. Climbing is great fun! It's a fab workout, in a social environment. Give it a go!
Can I just come along and boulder?
Absolutely! Most of us do roped climbing on these Tuesdays. If you prefer bouldering, you can sign yourself in and do it, as long as you can fill in the climbing centre's form correctly, watch their safety video and can answer the simple safety questions at reception on your first visit. Meet the group at the start; some others might be bouldering. And definitely come join us afterwards in the pub.
Participation Statement
IMPORTANT!
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Anyone with COVID-19 symptoms, even if they are extremely mild, or who has recently tested positive for Covid-19, is asked not to attend.
Can't make this event?
We run weekly climbing and bouldering events in the South East, so why not check out what's coming up near you here:
http://outdoorlads.events/SouthEastIndoorClimbing
. Alternatively, stay updated on upcoming events using the social media channels below:

(Climbing and bouldering only):
OutdoorLads (SE) Climbing
Facebook:
http://fb.com/OutdoorLadsSouthEast
Twitter:
@OdlSouthEast
Difficulty & Distance: With top-rope and lead climbs at every grade from complete beginner to seasoned pro, you decide how hard it gets!

Title: All Hale the Transpennine Trail
Summary:
Join Paul for a relaxed and social bike ride in Liverpool.
Starting in Central Liverpool we'll take advantage of the city's network of cycle paths and quieter roads, following National Cycle Network (NCN) Route 56 out to the Liverpool Loop Line, which is part of the
Transpennine Trail.
We'll follow the trail as far as the
Halewood Park Triangle
before making our way back to the start via Garston and Otterspool Promenade with it's fantastic waterside views.
Who’s It For?
This ride is perfect for all abilities - whether you're a relative beginner, a seasoned cyclist or just fancy  a casual spin with good company.
If you are driving to the event or local to Liverpool there is the option of meeting us near Otterspool where free parking is available. This will potentially knock several miles off the distance, depending on whether you decide to stay with the group as we continue along the Mersey back into the city centre. See
location
section for information about the alternative meeting place/time.
The route also offers options for leaving early and using public transport to get back to the city centre, for anyone who fancies a shorter ride.
Pace & Terrain
Speed
: 8 to 10 mph, always at the pace of the slowest rider—no one gets left behind. Depending on our pace, we'll be cycling for about 2.5 to 3 hours. The overall event timing is longer to allow for natural stops and starts, a quick break along the way and to enjoy a drink and maybe a bite to eat together at the end of the ride.
Route
: Mostly flat with some climbs, mixing roads, trails, and riverside paths.
Traffic
: Some (mainly quieter) roads—riders should feel comfortable cycling alongside traffic.
Bike & Rider Prep:
Best suited to hybrid bikes, the route is also doable on a road or mountain bike. The surfaces are mostly level/tarmac, with a cobbled section near the Albert Dock.
Ensure your bike is in good condition (inflated tyres, working brakes, oiled chain). The ride leader cannot provide repairs.
Bring a spare inner tube,
a packed lunch
for the break if you want one, snacks, and water.
Wear suitable comfortable clothing. Layers including something wind/water proof are recommended.
You must wear a
helmet
as this is one of OutdoorLads cycling participation requirements.
Weather Conditions
If extreme weather is forecast, we may postpone the ride. We’ll notify participants as early as possible.
All photos taken by OutdoorLads leaders and used with permission
Difficulty & Distance: A gentle leisure cycle - approx 23 miles with shorter options available

Title: Outwood Bound
Summary:
Join Paul on this leisurely bike ride from Manchester to Bolton and back.
Everyone (including beginners) is welcome. No one will get left behind. We'll ride at a gentle pace of 8 to 10 miles per hour for about 3 hours, but the event timing is longer to allow for the natural stops and starts of the ride, plus a short lunch stop in Bolton.
There are frequent trains between Bolton and Manchester, so there's the option of leaving/joining the ride in Bolton if you fancy a shorter cycle of less than 2 hours. If joining us from Bolton, please book onto the event as usual, then message our ride leader Paul for details of where to meet and the approximate meeting time.
Route information
Starting from Central Manchester, we will ride along National Cycle Network (NCN) Route 55 to Bolton. This follows roads with cycle lanes as far as Eccles (or there's a slightly longer off-road option along canal paths and dedicated cycle paths). We'll then use the quiet roads in the leafy suburb of Ellesmere Park to get to Monton. There we join the former Monton Green to Bolton Railway line, known as the Roe Green loop line which keeps us mainly off road until we reach the centre of Bolton.
Our return leg continues mainly off road to NCN Route 6 and the Outwood Trail, another former rail ay line running between Radclliffe and Prestwich. After passing through Drinkwater Park to the outskirts of Salford, we will keep following NCN Route 6 (which has on and off road options) back to the centre of Manchester.
Although much of the route is traffic free or on quieter roads, we may encounter the odd busy road. There will also be some fairly gentle climbs along the way. See the
location
section below for a link to the proposed route map and elevation chart.
The terrain is best suited to hybrid or mountain bikes, though it can be done on a road bike. Some parts of the trail are uneven and can be muddy if wet. Please check that your bike is roadworthy before the ride, as you will be responsible for dealing with your own mechanical issues, should they arise on the day.
Weather Conditions
Cold, wet and windy weather conditions aren't conducive to sociable cycling, and part of the route has been known to flood after very heavy rain. So, if the weather forecast for the day indicates extreme conditions, the event may be postponed with as much notice as possible provided to participants.

Title: Leisure Cycle - Goyt Valley & The Cat & Fiddle
Summary:
A leisurely social bike
ride
on a mixture of quiet lanes, rail trails canal towpaths to the Cat & Fiddle, until its closure, the second highest public house in the UK.
This is a rare opportunity to experience the descent of the main road between Buxton and Macclesfield almost traffic free due to the temporary closure for roadworks at  the Buxton end., The road descends from the Cat & Fiddle at 520m a.s.l to Macclesfield town centre over 11km, not quite all downhill as there is a short section of about 1km slightly uphill.
Starting from Marple, we follow the scenic Peak Forest Canal to its terminus at Whaley Bridge, where the climbing starts using some of the tramway used prior to the railways to transport quarried stone from the High Peak. We then follow a quiet lane to the Goyt Valley Reservoirs, passing them on bridleway and joining the road from Errwood to Derbyshire Bridge which is closed to traffic on Sundays. This is the main climb as the road ascends 250m over 6km to the Cat & Fiddle at over 500m above sea level
Weather permitting, we will have great views over Cheshire to the Welsh Hills, as we begin an exhilarating downhill as we descend over 400m over 11km.  From Macclesfield we return along the Middlewood Way, the former railway from Macclesfield to Marple
We have plenty of time to complete the route and we will take it at a relaxed pace and no one will be left behind.
Road cyclists:
Please be aware some paths might be a little rough and bumpy for thin tyres, but doable none the less. some sections of mud can be expected on the trails.
Mountain bikers:
Some of the route is on paved roads and expect to mix with traffic.
Pace and Terrain
This will be a leisurely cycle suitable for those of all levels of fitness. The majority of the route is on traffic free trails and quiet country lanes, but we do have about 11 miles on the old railway line and 7 miles on a canal towpath which can be muddy in places, but suitable for all bikes.
This event is open to cyclists of all abilities and bike types. Whilst there is a lot of climbing, it is all at relatively gentle gradients, but a reasonable level of fitness will be required.
If you're not a regular cyclist, please do make sure your bike is in good condition - check the tyres are well inflated, chain is oiled, and you've got a spare inner tube, drinks and snacks with you.
